doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Sitting next to Gene Krupa at a Benny Goodman gig in Washington
summary: Harry James takes two teenagers in at intermission and seats Fillius beside his idol Krupa; his father later caught the jazz bug.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: No. My father became so. He caught the bug. He caught the bug really during the war when he was playing my stuff he thought that’s not bad you know. And I was really hooked on it. I’ll tell you one story that remains bright in my mind. A friend of mine and I were in Washington, DC at my grandmother’s house and I think it was ’35 or ‘6, when the Spanish Civil War was going on, whenever the hell that was. And the Benny Goodman band was to play at the Raleigh Hotel in downtown Washington. And we decided we had to see that somehow. So we went down to the hotel in the daytime and welcomed the band when they came in. And Harry James went off in a side exit to smoke a cigarette. So we went out and talked to him and said, “Geez I sure would like to see that band. He said, “Well,” he says, “I’ll tell you what, meet me here at intermission and I’ll take you in.” So we did. We came down that night at intermission. James took us in, and he set me up right next to Krupa on the bandstand, who was my idol. And I had a wonderful time. And then Benny came in and gave me the ray you know. So we stayed a couple of sets and then we left. But that was the highlight of my youth.
